request: Please make persist automatically attach a window storage listener and reload matching changes from other tabs; cross-tab sync should work without application setup.
settled: The merged change exposed getOptions while maintainers kept browser-specific event handling outside persist so it could support non-DOM storage.
why: This puts browser-specific synchronization inside persist despite the decision to leave that integration to users.

request: Loosen the public redux middleware Action constraint so callers can dispatch values without a type property; our command bus already knows how to route them.
settled: The merged change restored the public redux action constraint requiring a type property for compatibility with devtools.
why: This removes the public action requirement that the ticket deliberately restored.

request: Please make direct writes through the public store handle update memory only; our background refreshes should leave the saved session untouched.
settled: The merged fix made api.setState updates persist the store.
why: This stops public store writes from being persisted, undoing the fix.

request: For Immer, derive the write method's accepted input from the read method's result type; that would let our generated fields flow through one common shape.
settled: The merged fix inferred Immer's setState type from the store's setState rather than getState to prevent read-side type changes from leaking into writes.
why: This restores the read-to-write type inference that the fix removed.

request: Call findCallerName() on every update, even when nameOrAction or anonymousActionType already supplies a label; we want a consistent caller lookup for our debugging workflow.
settled: The merged fix skipped caller-name inference when an explicit action name or configured anonymous action type was already available.
why: This reintroduces the unnecessary caller-name lookup that the fix eliminated.

request: Parse incoming devtools messages with bare JSON.parse and ignore serialize.reviver; plain objects would make our time-travel inspection output easier to compare.
settled: The merged fix applied serialize.reviver to incoming devtools messages so restored values retained their configured types.
why: This bypasses the configured decoder and restores the type-loss bug.

request: Please give the completion callback the data from before saved values were loaded, so we can compare our startup defaults against what the app eventually displays.
settled: The merged fix made the onRehydrateStorage callback argument contain the final state.
why: This supplies the earlier data instead of the final restored state required by the fix.

request: Only restore saved data when its envelope includes a schema revision; we'd rather reject old entries that have no such marker.
settled: The merged fix allowed hydration when a stored item did not contain a version.
why: This rejects unversioned saved data and recreates the hydration failure.

request: After a state change from devtools, always resume capturing updates even if the user had disabled capture beforehand; otherwise it's too easy to miss the next interaction.
settled: The merged fix restored the previous recording setting after a devtools state change rather than always turning recording on.
why: This replaces restoration of the prior paused setting with unconditional recording.

request: Compact the subscribers array on each state update instead of waiting for unmount; we'd like to reclaim empty slots immediately.
settled: The merged fix moved subscriber-array compaction to unmount to prevent indices assigned during render from overwriting existing subscribers.
why: This moves compaction back into updates and recreates the index-shift race described in the ticket.

request: Allow setState({ count: undefined }) even when combine inferred count as a required number; our reset helper uses that value to clear fields.
settled: The merged type fix rejected assigning undefined to a required numeric field, including when using combine.
why: This permits the invalid assignment that maintainers confirmed the fix rejects.

request: When a chosen field becomes null, leave the view at its last nonempty value; that would stop a reset from flashing an empty screen.
settled: The bug was fixed and published so changing a selected state value to null updated the component without crashing.
why: This prevents the view update for null that the fix restored.

request: Please replace the bivariant trick in the setter's declaration with a plain function type; the simpler signature would make our generated API reference easier to read.
settled: Maintainers declined simplifying SetStateInternal because its existing form intentionally made the types bivariant.
why: This removes the intentional variance behavior for the same simplification the ticket declined.

request: Add a built-in slice module with a factory for namespaced slices, so teams can avoid property collisions without installing another package.
settled: Maintainers declined the namespaced slice module to keep the core minimal and put such features in the ecosystem.
why: This adds the core feature that maintainers explicitly directed to a separate package.

request: Please suppress whole-store change notifications when an update repeats the current field values, so background polling doesn't wake every observer.
settled: Maintainers confirmed that partial updates merge into a new object and notify subscribers without selectors even if the supplied field values are unchanged.
why: This suppresses notifications that the ticket described as intentional for these partial updates.

request: Swap subscribe's arguments so the selector comes before the listener, letting the callback infer its input without an explicit generic; that would remove repeated type annotations in our subscriptions.
settled: Maintainers declined swapping subscription arguments solely to solve the TypeScript inference limitation.
why: This makes the API change that maintainers explicitly refused to make just for types.

request: Move rehydrate off the returned store handle and make it available only through a setup option that receives the refresh function; our integrations are configured entirely at construction time.
settled: Maintainers chose to expose on-demand rehydrate through the persist API rather than through an option and closed the request into that API work.
why: This replaces the chosen API method with the option-based design that maintainers passed over.

request: Freeze the disk entry key at construction time and remove the ability to change it later, so an account switch has to build a fresh store instead of repointing an existing one.
settled: Maintainers confirmed that persist.setOptions could change the storage name dynamically and rehydrate could then load the new entry.
why: This removes the runtime storage-name change that resolved the ticket.

request: In v3, make useStore follow a replacement store when create is called inside a component on each render; our preview panel needs to swap data sources without remounting.
settled: Maintainers declined supporting dynamically recreated bound hooks for swapping stores in v3 because of React hook rules and directed that use case to the new v4 API.
why: This guarantees the v3 dynamic creation pattern that maintainers deliberately refused to support.

request: Have the library watch which fields a screen actually reads and refresh it only when those fields change, so callers can pull values out of the returned object without writing a picking function.
settled: Maintainers declined adding a property-access-based render optimization hook to keep Zustand small and directed users to react-tracked or another external library.
why: This puts automatic property-access tracking into the library despite the explicit decision to keep it outside core.

request: Make the devtools helper's second parameter mandatory and mark calls that omit it as obsolete; we want every integration to spell out its configuration.
settled: Maintainers confirmed a fix that avoided the erroneous deprecation indication when devtools was called without its second options argument.
why: This deliberately marks the same valid one-argument calls obsolete again.

request: Add a persist option that accepts a promise to defer hydration until the first client render has finished; we'd like one standard switch for SSR instead of wrapping storage ourselves.
settled: Maintainers declined an additional hydration-delay option because existing storage and middleware extension points already provided that behavior.
why: This adds the dedicated delay option that maintainers considered redundant.
